blindSummary:
This country remains a low-danger destination for transgender visitors. A 2018 self-determination law allows legal gender and name change without medical requirements (minors 16-17 with parental consent), bathroom access matching one's gender is legally protected, conversion therapy is banned (2024), intersex infant surgery is banned, and hate-crime law covers gender identity — within a regional rule-of-law environment with very low violent crime. Same-sex marriage since 2010.

Two caveats temper the picture. First, in March 2026 the national parliament approved in first reading three bills (backed by the governing centre-right parties and the far right) that would repeal the 2018 self-ID law, reintroduce a mandatory medical opinion, and ban hormones for minors. As of the most recent reporting this is not yet final law — it is in committee, and a government technical opinion warned it may be unconstitutional — so the self-ID framework is still in force. Second, hate-crime reports rose about 38% in both 2023 and 2024, with acknowledged under-reporting.

For a visitor these translate to a real political-hostility signal and elevated but still low-level harassment risk, not criminal exposure. The practical day-to-day environment is calm and welcoming, particularly in the capital and the second city.
blindOutOfScope: Petty theft in tourist areas and a general terrorism guidance footnote affect all travellers.
blindSourceSummaries: A regional legal-rights index 2026 (May 2026): this country's neighbour tops the 49-country ranking; the index documents LGBTI human-rights laws and policies across the country's world region, with commentary on the gap between legal progress and daily experience.
National daily (March 2026): the national parliament approved governing-party and far-right bills reversing the gender-identity law - the first vote to roll back self-ID legal gender recognition.

News outlet (March 2026): the right moves to revoke the gender-identity regime - what may change and what each bill provides; governing and far-right parties voted to reverse the regime allowing gender change without medical validation; hormones for minors would be banned.

Joint statement (March 2026) by regional youth, intersex, trans and LGBTI organisations calling on this country's parliament to reject three bills attacking trans and intersex rights - a serious attack on rights, dignity, safety and bodily autonomy that would drop the country at least 4 places on the regional legal-rights index.

LGBTQ news site (March 2026): condemns the approval in general terms of three anti-trans bills (151-79), backed by the far right and the governing coalition; the bills target the 2018 self-identification law, would reintroduce medical gatekeeping, and one would ban discussing LGBTIQ+ topics in schools (mirroring 'anti-propaganda' laws in two other states).

Magazine (March 2026): this country set to roll back its trans self-determination law - the first-reading vote would reintroduce a mandatory medical opinion for legal gender/name change, undoing the 2018 reform (self-declaration from 16); human-rights groups warn of medicalised gatekeeping, delays, costs and arbitrary refusals.

TV and news agency (April 2026): the national equality commission confirms in a technical analysis that the current gender-identity law is aligned with international standards and that self-determination is protected by the constitution; the far-right bill 'rests on discontinued terminology' and non-consensual definitions.

News analysis (Aug 2026): legal gender changes edge back toward their 2024 record (606 in 2024, 541 in 2025; ~3,300 total since 2018), concentrated in the capital, as parliament moves to reimpose the medical test the 2018 self-determination law scrapped.

A written question to a regional parliament (2026), on the 'health and safety of transgender people': asks the regional executive about this country's parliamentary process to repeal its 2018 gender self-determination law and the health-and-safety impact on trans people.

Regional security-organisation page on this country's hate-crime legislation (a 1995 decree-law amended by a 2024 statute): excerpts including the aggravated-murder provision with SOGI-related aggravating circumstances.

Crowd-sourced safety data: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change with no restrictions, gender-affirming care legal, full ban on intersex infant surgery, hate-crime protections cover SOGI, discrimination illegal, conversion therapy banned, bathroom access protected. Highest public support for same-sex parenting of any of 30 regions in a continental survey.

National ombudsman: requests a review of the constitutionality of a penal-code provision establishing the crime of acts contrary to sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression - an unusual challenge to a protective provision.
blindLocalsOnly: The 2018 self-ID law, the 2026 repeal attempt (in committee), and the minors' hormone ban proposal are resident-facing; the intersex infant surgery ban is a resident protection.
blindTangential: Same-sex marriage since 2010 — relevant to trans visitors travelling with partners.
